title: Dual exterior-to-self-Tor comparison on regular affine charts
statement: For any closed immersion i:Z -> Y [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme], natural number n and derived category of module sheaves on Y [def-pc-derived-category], let B=i_*O_Z, C=i*ker(i) [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback] and Q=i*H^{-n}(B[0] tensor^L B[0]), using the fixed derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. There exists a global morphism tau: exteriorSheaf(C,n) -> Q [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. For every open V of Z and affine U of Y whose immersion ideal is spanned by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], the dual morphism dualMap(tau), restricted to V and then to the over site of V intersect i^{-1}(U), is an isomorphism [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No regularity of V or Y is assumed.

source.place: dpa.tex, lemma-divided-powers-on-tor: canonical strictly commutative Tor algebra from Tate resolutions. proof.text: Write B=i_*O_Z and Q=i*H^{-n}(B[0] tensor^L B[0]) using the fixed K-flat derived tensor. On an affine chart A with quotient B=A/I, tensor 0 -> I -> A -> B -> 0 with B. Its boundary identifies Tor_1^A(B,B) with I/I^2, with the map sending a conormal generator f to its degree-one resolution class. The actual kernel tensor-pullback has sections I/I^2 by the canonical pullback-unit comparison.

Construct the exterior-to-Tor map globally. Resolve an arbitrary quotient by a Tate strictly commutative dg algebra. Products of degree-one Tor classes are alternating, including in characteristic two, since odd elements square to zero. The exterior universal property supplies a map from exterior^n(I/I^2) to Tor_n(B,B). Resolution comparison preserves products and the boundary above. Flat localization commutes with this construction. Sheafifying these localization-compatible maps and using the quotient scalar action gives a global morphism tau: exteriorSheaf(i*ker(i),n) -> Q; no regularity and no choice of local isomorphisms is involved.

On a chart with m Koszul-regular generators use its Koszul projective resolution and sheafified augmentation to the quotient. Tensor with the quotient; all f_j vanish, so the differential is zero. The conormal classes are a basis. The Tor products of these classes are the increasing Koszul wedges, so tau is the corresponding exterior-basis isomorphism. The conormal frame identifies this calculation with the sheaf exterior power on the chart.

Dualize the chart isomorphism and restrict to arbitrary V and the over site of V intersect i^{-1}(U). Functors preserve inverses. For n=0 the map is the quotient unit. For n>m both sides are zero; m=0, the zero quotient and empty charts are included. No derived category on Z or on a restricted chart is added.

lean.statement:
theorem selfTor_conormal_dual_chart
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (n : ℕ) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let Q := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (-(n : ℤ))).obj
          (S.obj B ⊗ S.obj B))
    ∃ τ : Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules) n ⟶ Q,
      ∀ (V : Z.Opens) (U : Y.affineOpens)
        (_hU : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
          Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
            RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f),
        IsIso (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).map (Scheme.Modules.dualMap τ)).over
          (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))
